<role>
You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Need trial before commitment",
 "problem_statement": "Customers want to test key features like roles and tasks before signing up, because they need to be sure the platform fits their workflow before making a decision."
}
</opportunity>
<fact_sheet>
{
 "as_of": "2026-11-03",
 "accounts_n": 1,
 "mentions_n": 1,
 "routes_n": 1,
 "mentions_by_route": {
  "sales": 1
 },
 "arr_total_gbp": 0,
 "renewals_90d_n": 0,
 "accounts": [
  {
   "name": "Sallowmere Motor",
   "arr_gbp": null,
   "renewal_date": null,
   "mentions": 1
  }
 ]
}
</fact_sheet>
<insights>
[
 {
  "id": "fc502b52110e1c6b",
  "quote": "One last thing — can we trial the roles and tasks features before committing?",
  "account": "Sallowmere Motor",
  "route": "sales",
  "date": "2026-10-18T10:32:00Z"
 }
]
</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{
  "body_md": "## Problem
Customers evaluating Keelwater's claims-handling software are hesitant to commit to a purchase without first being able to test key platform functionality. They specifically need to validate that features like roles and tasks will integrate with and support their existing operational workflows before making a final decision.

## Who is affected
- At least 1 account, Sallowmere Motor, has directly requested a trial of specific features during the sales process [i:fc502b52110e1c6b].

## Evidence
- The fact sheet shows 1 account and 1 total mention of this need [i:fc502b52110e1c6b].
- The single mention occurred in the sales route [i:fc502b52110e1c6b].
- A customer, Sallowmere Motor, explicitly asked, One last thing — can we trial the roles and tasks features before committing? during a sales interaction on 2026-10-18 [i:fc502b52110e1c6b].
- The fact sheet records 0 accounts with a renewal in the last 90 days and 0 GBP in total ARR, indicating this is a request from a prospective, not an existing, customer.

## Why now
The request was made during a recent sales conversation on 2026-10-18 [i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. The fact that this is the only customer mention recorded as of 2026-11-03, and it originated from the sales route, suggests this is a current barrier to conversion for at least one prospective account in the active sales pipeline.",
  "citations": ["fc502b52110e1c6b"]
}
